memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses saw that the people were running wild and that Aaron had let them get out of control and so become a laughing-stock to their enemies. So he stood at the entrance to the camp and said, 'Whoever is for the Lord, come to me.' And all the Levites rallied to him." - Exod 32:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Aaron had let them get out of control." That is the verdict on passive leadership. Aaron did not push them into sin; he simply removed the restraint.

Then comes the moment that cuts through everything: "Whoever is for the Lord, come to me." No debate. No committee. A line drawn in the sand and a call to step across it.

There are seasons when God brings us to exactly such a moment. Not a gentle nudge, but a clear call requiring a visible decision. Joshua would later say, "Choose this day whom you will serve" (Josh 24:15). Elijah would ask how long the people would waver between two opinions (1 Kgs 18:21).

The Levites moved. They did not have more information than anyone else. They simply responded.

Jesus made the same kind of call — leave your nets, follow me (Mark 1:17-18). Discipleship always involves a step that others can see. Faith that never costs anything, never shows anything, and never separates us from the crowd may not be faith at all.

Where is God asking you to step across the line?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a decision for God you have been putting off?
2. What restraints in your life have you quietly let go?
3. Who would notice if you publicly stood for Christ this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I am for You. Give me courage to say so clearly and to live it visibly. Amen.
